newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan lowers mooring charges at major ports.
newsitem.headline: Japan lowers mooring charges at major ports.

text.p: In a move that may ease recent tensions between United States and Japanese shipping authorities, Japan has slashed mooring fees at about 20 major ports by some 25 percent, shipping officials said on Thursday.

Japanese authorities decided in early March to cut charges imposed on visiting vessels, shortly after the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission announced plans to levy a $100,000 surcharge on Japanese shipping companies each time their vessels entered a U.S. port from abroad.
The U.S. threat was advanced amid charges that Japanese port practices unfairly discriminated against foreign carriers.

Pressure had also been applied by the European Union, which last October called for consultations with Japan under World Trade Organisation rules to make Japanese ports more accessible to foreign shippers.
"The number of ports making the change is around 20 at this point," an official from the Transport Ministry's Port Division said.
Among the ports affected are Tokyo, Yokohama, Kobe, Kawasaki, Osaka, Shimonoseki, Kitakyushu and Nagoya.

Under the new system, vessels will be charged 10.05 yen per hour per gross registered tonne (grt) for vessels docking up to 12 hours. An additional 6.75 yen per hour will be added for every 12 hours thereafter.

Formerly, vessels were charged a flat minimum fee for moorings up to 24 hours regardless of the length of stay. The fee was equivalent to an hourly rate of 13.4 yen per gross registered tonne. Vessels such as container ships and pure car carriers, which are used increasingly, are usually loaded or unloaded in less than 24 hours.
